title: Dynamic Surge Capacity Compactor and Utilization Signal Federation
author: Maya Thompson
description: Motivation: short, high-frequency microbursts from multi-tenant workloads cause the autoscaler to over-reserve GPU capacity or keep ephemeral warmlets alive longer than needed, increasing unit cost and fragmenting capacity. This PR introduces a "compactor" layer in the Dedicated fleet allocator that coalesces short-duration surge allocations into a pooled short-lived reserve and a utilization signal federation that combines node-level quantile signals to avoid noisy single-host spikes. Implementation summary: add compactor controller (server-side) that tracks ephemeral allocations with metadata (tenant, requested_rps, started_at) and applies compaction rules (min_duration_ms, max_compact_window_ms, tenant_safety_floor) before committing backend reservations; introduce a federated utilization estimator which computes p50/p75/p95/p99 per-tenant and per-region using ring-aggregated histograms and exposes aggregated metrics to the console; integrate compactor decisions with the autoscaler to permit transient pooled draws without altering tenant persistent reservations; add runtime feature flags and Helm values to enable staged rollout. Backwards compatibility and safety: compactor is disabled by default; when enabled it operates under conservative defaults (min_duration_ms=500, max_compact_window_ms=15000, max_compacted_fraction=0.15) and includes automatic fallbacks to the pre-compaction path if reclaim latency or observed SLA regressions exceed thresholds. Telemetry: new metrics rwi_compactor_allocations_total, rwi_compactor_reclaims_total, rwi_compactor_compacted_duration_ms_bucket, rwi_federated_util_p50/p75/p95/p99 with tenant/region labels and a cardinality cap via label whitelisting; audit events emitted for every compaction action for compliance. Testing and validation: unit tests for compactor allocator and histogram merger, integration tests exercising the autoscaler+compactor across synthetic microburst workloads, a perf-canary that ran across two staging clusters with 72-hour stress and produced a 12% reduction in reserved-gpu-hours and no measurable increase in 99th percentile latency. Rollout plan: staged enablement (1% of Dedicated slots in us-west for 48h, then 10% for 72h, then 100% regionally) with automatic rollback on SLA regressions tracked by PM-221; feature flag and Helm chart toggles included for rapid disabled deployment. Related work: builds on ENG-4593 (surge footprinter) and ENG-4601 (warmlet prewarming improvements).

review_comments: Amit Gupta: Safety first—what's the rollback surface if compaction causes a steady increase in reclaim rate?

Maya Thompson: Added automatic throttling in compactor (backpressure on compaction) and a reclamation spillover detector; compactor will stop compacting for a tenant if reclaim_rate > 0.02 over 5m and will emit an audit event.
Sofia Rivera: Metric cardinality risk—tenant labels on p99 could explode. How do we limit?
Maya Thompson: We added a label whitelist and a global cardinality cap with a sampled fallback; documented in docs/designs/compactor.md and enforced in the exporter layer.
Liam O'Connor: Can we make the min_duration_ms configurable per-tenant? Some customers have known microburst patterns.
Maya Thompson: Exposed an opt-in per-tenant override via the Dedicated tenant profile API; default remains global conservative value.
Sofia Rivera: Approved pending test flake fix and a short section in the runbook on how to interpret compactor metrics for on-call.
Maya Thompson: Added runbook snippet and fixed the timing flake by increasing the test harness clock granularity; CI green now.
release_notes: Introduce a conservative, opt-in compactor for short-duration surge allocations and a federated utilization estimator. Expected benefit: reduced reserved GPU-hours for microbursty tenants and improved packing. Disabled by default; enable via Helm or feature flag. See docs/designs/compactor.md for config and runbook.
notes: Perf canary results attached in build artifacts; operations notified and a post-merge rollout was scheduled per PM-221.
